chunks: From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for a garment, measured it, and took five cubits from it, then cut it. Then he measured its width as six shibars (open-palm widths). Then he split it and said, 'Stitch its sides and trim its edges.'

key_terms.أَشْبَارٍ: shibars (plural of shibr, an open-palm width)

ai.seo_question: What are the prescribed dimensions for the length and width of a garment according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific tailoring of the Imam’s garment, establishing a physical standard for modesty and distinction in attire. It highlights the practical application of the principle of 'hadd' (limit/measure) in Islamic jurisprudence, where precise dimensions guide the permissibility and style of clothing. The instruction to 'bind the sides' and 'trim the edges' underscores the importance of neatness and completeness in fulfilling the Sunnah of dress.
